title_en: Shanghai Huangpu District People's Procuratorate v. Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo — theft case
ruling_gist_en: Where an actor rents out a bank card to another person for use, and after the renter changes the bank card password, the bank card is swallowed by an ATM due to careless use. The actor, with the purpose of illegal possession, takes advantage of the renter's request for assistance in retrieving the card, and while the renter knows the password and actually possesses and controls the deposit in the bank card, uses means such as reporting loss and reissuing a card to withdraw and appropriate the renter's deposit in the bank card. Such conduct constitutes secretly stealing another person's property and shall be convicted and punished as the crime of theft.

full_text_en:
Shanghai Huangpu District People's Procuratorate v. Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo — Theft

Ruling Summary

Where a person rents a bank card to another for use, and after the renter changes the bank card password, the bank card is swallowed by an ATM due to careless use, and the cardholder, with the intent of illegal possession, takes advantage of the renter's request for assistance in retrieving the card, and while the renter knows the password and actually possesses and controls the deposits in the card, uses means such as reporting the loss and applying for a replacement card to withdraw and appropriate the renter's deposits in the card, the conduct constitutes the secret theft of another's property and shall be convicted and punished as theft.

Procuratorial Authority: Shanghai Huangpu District People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Cui Yong, male, 31 years old, unemployed, temporarily residing at Qinnan Town, Yandu District, Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province. Arrested on December 4, 2009 for this case.

Defendant: Qiu Guobin, male, 24 years old, farmer, residing at Yifeng Town, Yandu District, Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province. Arrested on December 4, 2009 for this case.

Defendant: Zhang Zhiguo, male, 33 years old, farmer, temporarily residing at Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province. Arrested on December 4, 2009 for this case.

The Shanghai Huangpu District People's Procuratorate instituted a public prosecution with the Shanghai Huangpu District People's Court against Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo for theft.

The indictment charged that: Defendant Qiu Guobin, accompanied by Luo Changying, went to a bank with his own identity card to apply for an e-era card bundled with a bank POS terminal, and later this card was placed under the custody of Defendant Cui Yong. Through Luo Changying's introduction, Cui Yong rented this card to the victim, Mou Chimin, for use. When Mou Chimin used the card at a bank ATM, the card was swallowed due to careless operation. Mou Chimin then asked Luo Changying to contact Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin to help retrieve the card from the bank. After consulting with Qiu Guobin and Defendant Zhang Zhiguo, Cui Yong had Qiu Guobin go to the bank to report the loss of the card and apply for a replacement new card, and then through withdrawals and transfers, they misappropriated RMB 298,742.09 stored by Mou Chimin in the card, and the three defendants divided the money among themselves. Cui Yong, in collusion with Qiu Guobin and Zhang Zhiguo, with the intent of illegal possession, jointly and secretly stole another's property in an especially huge amount. Their conduct has violated Article 264 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law) and constitutes theft. Please investigate and affix the criminal liability of the three defendants according to law. This case is a joint crime, subject to Article 25, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law; among them, Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin are principals, subject to Articles 26, paragraphs 1 and 4 of the Criminal Law, and shall be punished for all crimes in which they participated or which they organized or directed; Zhang Zhiguo is an accessory, subject to Article 27 of the Criminal Law, and shall be given a lighter or mitigated punishment.

Defendants Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin did not object to the facts alleged in the indictment.

Defendant Zhang Zhiguo argued: He had always believed that the money in the bank card involved was owned by Defendant Qiu Guobin himself, and he never conspired with Cui Yong to persuade Qiu Guobin to transfer the remaining balance to Cui Yong. As for the money that Cui Yong gave him, part was repayment of a debt owed by Cui Yong, and part was a loan from Cui Yong to him. Therefore, his conduct did not constitute theft.

The defense counsels for the three defendants argued: Theft involves taking property under another's control or possession into one's own possession. The bank card involved was applied for by Defendant Qiu Guobin using his own identity card in his real name. The money taken by the three defendants was stored in the card involved and was possessed by Qiu Guobin. The victim, Mou Chimin, asked Qiu Guobin to go to the bank to retrieve the card because it was swallowed due to careless operation; therefore, a civil principal-agent relationship was formed between the victim and Qiu Guobin, and in this process, Qiu Guobin was obligated to take custody of the new card. At that time, the bank card involved and the deposits therein were under the actual control of Qiu Guobin. Hence, the conduct of the three defendants does not meet the characteristic of "transfer of possession" required for theft; the acts of reporting loss and applying for a replacement card by the three defendants were carried out openly at the victim's request and under his mandate, and the procedures were lawful. Moreover, when the card was swallowed and the victim could not contact the three defendants, he already knew that the money in the card might be taken by the three defendants. Therefore, the acts of reporting loss, applying for a replacement card, and withdrawing money by the three defendants lacked the element of secrecy because the victim had actually become aware of them. In summary, all three defense counsels believed that this case did not constitute theft.

The Shanghai Huangpu District People's Court found from the first-instance trial:

In April 2009, Defendant Qiu Guobin entrusted Defendant Cui Yong to help him apply for a bank credit card that could be overdrawn in Shanghai, and gave his identity card and other documents to Cui Yong. In May of the same year, Cui Yong notified Qiu Guobin to come to Shanghai, and accompanied by Luo Changying, they applied for an e-era card with card number 6222021001015592865, bundled with a bank POS terminal, in Qiu Guobin's name. The card was kept by Cui Yong. In early June, Cui Yong rented the card to the victim, Mou Chimin, through Luo Changying. In late June, when Mou Chimin used the card at a bank ATM, it was swallowed due to careless operation. Mou Chimin then asked Luo Changying to request Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin to help retrieve the card. Upon learning of this, Cui Yong discussed with Qiu Guobin and Defendant Zhang Zhiguo, and they decided that Qiu Guobin would go to the bank to report the loss and take the opportunity to misappropriate the money in the card. Zhang Zhiguo and Qiu Guobin both agreed.

At the end of June of the same year, the victim Mou Chimin and Luo Changying, unable to contact Defendants Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin, drove to the hometowns of Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin to look for them but failed. They then asked Qiu Guobin's relatives to tell Qiu Guobin that the money in the card was earned by Mou Chimin through business and that touching it would be illegal. That evening, Qiu Guobin's girlfriend, Chen Ya, called Qiu Guobin and told him that there was about RMB 300,000 in the card involved and that Mou Chimin had come to their hometown looking for Qiu Guobin, asking him not to use the money in the card. When Qiu Guobin received the call, both Cui Yong and Zhang Zhiguo were present.

On July 2 of the same year, Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo went to the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Co., Ltd., Yanchang Middle Road Sub-branch in Shanghai (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Yanchang Sub-branch). Qiu Guobin handled the procedures for reporting the loss of the bank card involved and applying for a replacement card. Since it would take seven days to receive the new card after the replacement application, the three defendants left Shanghai that day and returned to Suzhou, with all expenses during this period borne by Zhang Zhiguo. On July 9, the three defendants again came to ICBC Yanchang Sub-branch. Qiu Guobin handled the procedures to receive the new card, with the new card number being 6222021001032908011, and containing RMB 298,742.09. Subsequently, the three defendants went to the ICBC Yanchang New Village Sub-branch at No. 790 Yanchang Middle Road, Shanghai, and withdrew RMB 68,700 in cash. Qiu Guobin and Zhang Zhiguo each received RMB 10,000, and Cui Yong took the remainder. At the same time, Cui Yong immediately applied for an e-era card with card number 6222021001026089901 in his own name. The three defendants then rushed to the ICBC People's Square Sub-branch at No. 377 West Nanjing Road, Shanghai. After persuasion by Cui Yong and Zhang Zhiguo, Qiu Guobin transferred the remaining balance of RMB 230,000 in the card to Cui Yong's new card. Thereafter, the three fled Shanghai. Cui Yong then gave another RMB 10,000 each to Qiu Guobin and Zhang Zhiguo, and transferred RMB 50,000 to the bank account of Zhou Li, Zhang Zhiguo's former wife.

On October 28, 2009, Defendant Qiu Guobin voluntarily surrendered to the public security authorities in his place of origin. On November 4, 2009, Defendant Zhang Zhiguo was captured by the public security authorities in Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province. While Defendant Cui Yong was undergoing compulsory drug rehabilitation, he was identified and captured by the public security authorities through online comparison information on November 5, 2009.

After the case was discovered, Cui Yong's family returned RMB 10,000; Qiu Guobin returned one ring purchased with the illicit gains; and Zhang Zhiguo's former wife Zhou Li returned RMB 35,000.

The above facts were confirmed by the testimony of the victim Mou Chimin; the testimony of witness Luo Changying and the identification笔录; the testimony of witnesses Chen Ya and Zhou Li; the transaction details and merchant stubs of the e-era card involved; the relevant documentary evidence regarding the loss report, application, cash withdrawal, and deposit transfer; the list of seized items from the Shanghai Municipal Public Security Bureau; the explanations from the public security authorities regarding the circumstances of the arrest of Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo; and the confessions of the three defendants, among other evidence. It was sufficient to establish.

The focus of dispute in the first-instance trial was whether the conduct of Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo constituted theft or embezzlement.

The Shanghai Huangpu District People's Court held in the first instance:

1. Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo subjectively had the intent to illegally possess another's property.

Based on the in-court statements of Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo, the testimony of the victim Mou Chimin, and the testimony of witnesses Luo Changying and Chen Ya, it can be determined that all three defendants knew that the money in the bank card involved, held in Qiu Guobin's name, did not belong to Qiu Guobin but was personal property stored by Mou Chimin. When the bank card involved was swallowed and Mou Chimin requested Qiu Guobin to help retrieve it, the three defendants did not assist in retrieving the card and returning it to Mou Chimin. Instead, they actively engaged in reporting the loss, applying for a replacement card, withdrawing money, and transferring funds, dividing the money in the card among themselves. This clearly showed an intent to illegally possess another's property.

2. The conduct of Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo had the nature of secret theft.

Based on the facts of this case, there existed a special lease relationship between Defendants Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin and the victim Mou Chimin, with the POS terminal and the e-era card as the subject matter. That is, the e-era card involved, which was bundled with the POS terminal, was under Qiu Guobin's name but was rented to Mou Chimin for use. Due to Mou Chimin's operational error, the card was swallowed, and he requested Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin to help retrieve the card. Thereafter, when Mou Chimin could not contact Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin through Luo Changying, Mou Chimin had a premonition that the money in the card might be taken by Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin. Moreover, when he confirmed through inquiry that the money in the card had been transferred, Mou Chimin immediately concluded that it was the act of Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and others. Based on this, the defense counsels for the three defendants argued that the acts of reporting loss, applying for a replacement card, and withdrawing money by the three defendants lacked the element of secrecy because the victim had actually become aware of them. The court held that the above circumstances do not affect the secret theft nature of the three defendants' conduct. "Secret theft" in the crime of theft refers to conduct where the actor, using means that the actor believes will not be discovered by the owner or custodian of the property at the time, and contrary to the will of the owner or custodian, transfers the property to the possession of oneself or a third party. "Secret theft" in the crime of theft has the characteristics of subjectivity, relativity, and contemporaneity. Subjectivity means that the actor subjectively believes that the theft will not be discovered; whether it is actually discovered does not affect the establishment of "secret theft". Relativity means that the actor believes that the theft will not be discovered by the owner or custodian of the property; whether it is discovered by a third party does not affect the establishment of "secret theft". Contemporaneity means that the actor believes that the theft will not be discovered at the time of its commission; whether it is discovered afterwards does not affect the establishment of "secret theft". In this case, although the three defendants openly carried out the acts of reporting loss, applying for a replacement card, withdrawing money, and transferring funds, the victim did not discover them at the time, much less could he prevent the three defendants' actions. Although the victim had suspicions and conjectures that the three defendants might infringe upon his property and became aware of the three defendants' criminal conduct immediately after the incident, this is fundamentally different from discovering the criminal conduct at the scene. Therefore, the conduct of the three defendants fully meets the characteristic of "secret theft" in the crime of theft. The defense counsels' arguments cannot be established and are not adopted.

3. The conduct of Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo meets the legal characteristic of "transfer of possession" in the crime of theft.

In this case, after the victim Mou Chimin rented the e-era card involved, which was bundled with the POS terminal, from Defendant Qiu Guobin, he changed the password. By holding the bank card involved and knowing the password, he formed an actual possession and control over the money in the card. Thereafter, although the card was swallowed due to operational error, the victim, based on his knowledge of the password, still maintained actual control over the money in the card. After the card was swallowed, Mou Chimin requested Defendants Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin through Luo Changying to help retrieve the card. The content of this request was clearly limited to retrieving the card and did not involve entrusting the custody of the money in the card. During this period, Mou Chimin explicitly asked Qiu Guobin's girlfriend to tell Qiu Guobin not to use the money in the card, and Qiu Guobin's girlfriend truthfully conveyed Mou Chimin's request to Qiu Guobin. Therefore, it can be determined that Mou Chimin never expressed any intention to entrust the custody of the money in the card to the defendants, and the three defendants knew this. The defense counsels' argument that a civil principal-agent relationship was formed when the victim requested Qiu Guobin to go to the bank to retrieve the card, and that the bank card involved and the deposits therein therefore came under Qiu Guobin's actual control, cannot be established.

As discussed earlier, after the bank card involved was swallowed, although the victim Mou Chimin lost actual control over the card, based on his knowledge of the password, he did not lose possession and control over the money in the card. If Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo had merely assisted the victim in retrieving the bank card involved, they could not have controlled the money in the card. The three defendants achieved control and possession of the money in the bank card involved by actively engaging in acts such as reporting the loss, applying for a replacement new card, and transferring funds. The above conduct fully meets the legal characteristic of "transfer of possession" in the crime of theft. The defense counsels' argument that the money in the bank card involved was possessed and controlled by Qiu Guobin and that the conduct of the three defendants did not have the nature of "transfer of possession" cannot be established and is not adopted.

In summary, Defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo, with the intent of illegal possession, jointly and secretly stole another's property in an especially huge amount. Their conduct has all constituted the crime of theft as provided for in Article 264 of the Criminal Law and shall be subject to criminal punishment. The charge of theft brought by the Procuratorial Authority against Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo is established. The three defendants intentionally committed the criminal act jointly. Pursuant to Article 25, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, it constitutes a joint crime, and they shall jointly bear corresponding criminal liability. Among them, Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin played a principal role in the joint crime and are principals. Pursuant to Articles 26, paragraphs 1 and 4 of the Criminal Law, they shall be punished for all crimes in which they participated. Zhang Zhiguo played a secondary role in the joint crime and is an accessory. Pursuant to Article 27 of the Criminal Law, he shall be given a mitigated punishment. The relevant defense opinions of Zhang Zhiguo's defense counsel are adopted. Upon investigation, when Zhang Zhiguo was first interrogated after his arrest, he admitted that he knew the nature of the money in the bank card involved, and stated that his participation in the crime was because Cui Yong had promised to give him one-third of the money after the matter was completed. Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin repeatedly stated that Zhang Zhiguo had persuaded Qiu Guobin to transfer the remaining balance in the card to Cui Yong. Zhang Zhiguo's defense that the money he received was repayment of a debt by Cui Yong and a loan from Cui Yong to him was not corroborated by Cui Yong, nor could he provide corresponding evidence. Therefore, Zhang Zhiguo's relevant defenses cannot be established and are not adopted. Qiu Guobin voluntarily surrendered and, pursuant to Article 67, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, may be given a mitigated punishment. Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin had a good attitude of admitting guilt and were able to truthfully confess their crimes during the trial; a lighter punishment may be given at discretion. The criminal gains of the three defendants shall, pursuant to Article 64 of the Criminal Law, be recovered and returned to the victim.

Accordingly, the Shanghai Huangpu District People's Court, pursuant to Article 264, Article 25, paragraph 1, Article 26, paragraphs 1 and 4, Article 27, Article 67, paragraph 1, and Article 64 of the Criminal Law, rendered judgment on July 12, 2010 as follows:

1. Defendant Cui Yong is convicted of theft and sentenced to ten years' imprisonment, and shall also be fined RMB 10,000.
2. Defendant Qiu Guobin is convicted of theft and sentenced to six years' imprisonment, and shall also be fined RMB 6,000.
3. Defendant Zhang Zhiguo is convicted of theft and sentenced to seven years' imprisonment, and shall also be fined RMB 7,000.
4. The illegal gains shall be recovered according to law and returned to the victim.

Zhang Zhiguo, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, claiming that he did not know that the money in the bank card involved was not owned by the original defendant Qiu Guobin himself, that he did not conspire with the original defendant Cui Yong and others to commit the theft, and that his role in the case was minor, requesting a lighter punishment.

After the second-instance trial, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance:

Based on the facts of this case, after the original defendants Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and the appellant Zhang Zhiguo learned of the victim Mou Chimin's request for help in retrieving the bank card involved, they immediately discussed misappropriating the money stored by the victim in the bank card involved through means such as reporting the loss and applying for a replacement new card. Subsequently, when Mou Chimin asked Qiu Guobin's girlfriend to tell Qiu Guobin not to touch the money in the card, Cui Yong, Qiu Guobin, and Zhang Zhiguo were all present. Therefore, Zhang Zhiguo's appeal that he did not know that the money in the card was not owned by Qiu Guobin and that he did not conspire with Cui Yong and Qiu Guobin to steal the money is inconsistent with the facts and is not adopted. The original judgment had clear factual findings, correct application of law, appropriate sentencing, and lawful trial procedures, and should be affirmed.

Accordingly, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 189, paragraph (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the ruling on September 7, 2010 as follows:

Appeal dismissed; original judgment sustained.

This ruling is final.
